newsitem.title: USA: MCI wins US Postal network management deal.
newsitem.headline: MCI wins US Postal network management deal.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp said the U.S. Postal Service had agreed to a five-year Managed Network Services (MNS) contract with a guaranteed value of at least $100 million and a potential value of up to $3 billion.
The network management contract calls for MCI to provide the Postal Service an array of telecommunications services and represents MCI's largest contract award to date, it said.

The five-year deal has two three-year renewal options that could allow the contract to run for up to 11 years. As part of the deal, MCI will establish and manage a telecommunications network to connect up to 34,000 Postal Service locations.
MCI was the lead contractor on the deal. Other suppliers on the network contract team include Cisco Systems Inc, DynCorp I&ET Inc, Digital Equipment Corp and JIL Information Systems Inc.
The award is an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract, the company said.
MCI said the managed network operations will improve post office customer service by streamlining operations and creating mechanisms for providing new types of services.

The managed network program will improve the Postal Service's access to data and information across multiple computer systems, provide centralized software distribution and help-desk technical support.
"The MCI network will give us the availability and responsiveness we need to meet our customers' expectations," said Rick Weirich, vice president of information services for the Postal Service.
